# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles population estimates for 8.064 cities, industrial towns, railway junctions and ports across the 48 provinces of Late Imperial Russia and Austro-Hungarian Ukraine at five benchmark dates between the Congress of Vienna in 1815AD and the Russian Revolution of 1917AD. Before the emancipation of the serfs in the 1860s, urban growth remained modest outside Saint Petersburg, Moscow, Warsaw, Odessa and Riga. Over the next half-century, railway building, coal and steel works in the Donbas and Congress Poland, the Grozny and Boryslav oil booms and peasant migration along the Trans-Siberian line transformed the urban map. By 1914AD, Saint Petersburg (2,12M) and Moscow (1,76M) led an urban network that included Warsaw (884,5k), Odessa (630k), Kyiv (626,3k), Riga (517,5k) and the textile and mining boomtowns of Lodz (477,9k), Sosnowiec (118,5k) and Yuzovka (54k), before the First World War emptied frontline cities in Poland, Courland and Lithuania and swelled interior towns with more than 6M refugees [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @Gatrell1999].

# Methodology

This gazetteer traces the population histories of 8.064 towns, industrial centres, ports and fortresses across the 48 provinces of Late Imperial Russia and Austro-Hungarian Ukraine (excluding Central Asia and the Southern Caucasus) from the Congress of Vienna in 1815AD to the revolutions of 1917AD. Each town is listed under its historical name alongside its local and modern equivalents, geographic coordinates and population estimates for 1815AD, 1858AD, 1897AD, 1914AD and 1917AD.

The town figures draw on the main fiscal and statistical surveys of the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries: the Seventh (1815-1816AD), Eighth (1833-1835AD) and Tenth (1857-1858AD) Imperial Soul Revisions and Ministry of Internal Affairs town tables [@Troinitsky1861; @Kabuzan1971; @Rashin1956], the First All-Russian General Census of 28 January 1897AD across all 89 provincial volumes and its companion register of settlements over 500 inhabitants [@Troinitsky1905; @Troinitsky1905Goroda], the 1 January 1914AD yearbooks of the Central Statistical Committee and the Warsaw Statistical Committee [@TsSK1915; @WarsawStat1914], the ten-year censuses of the Finnish Statistical Office [@FinlandStat1870_1915], the Austrian and Hungarian censuses of 1869-1910AD for Galicia, Bukovina and Subcarpathia [@OsterreichischeStatistik1912; @MagyarStatisztika1912] and the 1916-1917AD All-Russian Urban and Agricultural Censuses paired with Tatiana Committee wartime refugee records [@AgCensus1917; @Gatrell1999]. Industrial, coal-mining, railway and northern ports founded after 1815AD - such as Bodaibo (1864AD), Yuzovka (1869AD), Novonikolaevsk (1893AD), Belotsarsk (1914AD) and Romanov-on-Murman (1916AD) - are marked `-` at dates prior to their establishment.



# Results

## Warsaw, Plock and Lomza Governorates

Table \ref{tab:reg1-sites} gives the populations of the 86 catalogued settlements in the Warsaw, Plock and Lomza governorates, where the regional population grew from 1,02M in 1815AD to 3,54M in 1897AD and 5,05M in 1914AD before falling to 4,42M in 1917AD during the First World War [@WarsawStat1914; @Troinitsky1905Goroda; @Corrsin1989; @Gatrell1999].

## Piotrkow and Kalisz Governorates

Table \ref{tab:reg2-sites} gives the populations of the 39 catalogued settlements in the Piotrkow and Kalisz governorates, where the regional population rose from 720k in 1815AD to 2,25M in 1897AD and 3,32M in 1914AD before dropping to 2,95M in 1917AD [@WarsawStat1914; @Troinitsky1905Goroda; @Corrsin1989; @Gatrell1999].

## Lublin and Siedlce Governorates

Table \ref{tab:reg3-sites} gives the populations of the 36 catalogued settlements in the Lublin and Siedlce governorates (including the 1912AD Kholm Governorate), where the regional population grew from 780k in 1815AD to 1,93M in 1897AD and 2,68M in 1914AD before the 1915AD evacuation reduced it to 2,08M in 1917AD [@WarsawStat1914; @Troinitsky1905Goroda; @Corrsin1989; @Gatrell1999].

## Radom, Kielce and Suwalki Governorates

Table \ref{tab:reg4-sites} gives the populations of the 59 catalogued settlements in the Radom, Kielce and Suwalki governorates, where the regional population grew from 780k in 1815AD to 2,16M in 1897AD and 2,6M in 1914AD before falling to 2,18M in 1917AD [@WarsawStat1914; @Troinitsky1905Goroda; @Corrsin1989; @Gatrell1999].

## Courland Governorate

Table \ref{tab:reg7-sites} gives the populations of the 42 catalogued settlements in Courland Governorate, where the regional population rose from 418k in 1815AD to 674k in 1897AD and 800k in 1914AD before the 1915AD German occupation and refugee flight halved it to 380k in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Gortfelder2023BalticFertility; @Gatrell1999].

## Southern Finland: Nyland, Abo-Bjorneborg, Tavastehus and Vyborg

Table \ref{tab:reg8-sites} gives the populations of the 78 catalogued settlements in southern Finland (Nyland, Abo-Bjorneborg, Tavastehus and Vyborg provinces), where the regional population grew from 590k in 1815AD to 1,43M in 1897AD, 1,84M in 1914AD and 1,89M in 1917AD [@FinlandStat1870_1915; @Pitkanen1993; @Luostarinen2026FinlandMortality].

## Interior and Northern Finland: Vasa, Kuopio, Sankt-Michel and Uleaborg

Table \ref{tab:reg9-sites} gives the populations of the 46 catalogued settlements in interior and northern Finland (Vasa, Kuopio, Sankt-Michel and Uleaborg provinces), where the regional population rose from 520k in 1815AD to 1,13M in 1897AD, 1,4M in 1914AD and 1,43M in 1917AD [@FinlandStat1870_1915; @Pitkanen1993; @Luostarinen2026FinlandMortality].

## Kovno Governorate

Table \ref{tab:reg10-sites} gives the populations of the 96 catalogued settlements in Kovno Governorate, where the regional population grew from 660k in 1815AD to 1,54M in 1897AD and 1,84M in 1914AD before falling to 1,32M in 1917AD during the First World War [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rowland1986; @Gatrell1999].

## Vilna and Grodno Governorates

Table \ref{tab:reg11-sites} gives the populations of the 139 catalogued settlements in the Vilna and Grodno governorates, where the regional population grew from 1,15M in 1815AD to 3,19M in 1897AD and 3,94M in 1914AD before the 1915AD retreat reduced it to 2,88M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rowland1986; @Gatrell1999].

## Minsk Governorate and Pripyat Polesia

Table \ref{tab:reg12-sites} gives the populations of the 108 catalogued settlements in Minsk Governorate, where the regional population grew from 920k in 1815AD to 2,15M in 1897AD and 3,04M in 1914AD before dipping to 2,89M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rowland1986; @Gatrell1999].

## Vitebsk and Mogilev Governorates

Table \ref{tab:reg13-sites} gives the populations of the 107 catalogued settlements in the Vitebsk and Mogilev governorates, where the regional population grew from 1,25M in 1815AD to 3,18M in 1897AD and 4,02M in 1914AD before edging down to 3,86M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rowland1986; @Gatrell1999].

## Austro-Hungarian Eastern Galicia

Table \ref{tab:reg14-sites} gives the populations of the 185 catalogued settlements in Eastern Galicia, where the regional population grew from 2,58M in 1815AD to 4,42M in 1897AD and 5,02M in 1914AD before fighting on the Carpathian and Galician fronts reduced it to 4,45M in 1917AD [@OsterreichischeStatistik1912; @MagyarStatisztika1912; @Himka1988; @Gatrell1999].

## Austro-Hungarian Bukovina and Subcarpathian Rus

Table \ref{tab:reg15-sites} gives the populations of the 122 catalogued settlements in Bukovina and Subcarpathian Rus, where the regional population rose from 770k in 1815AD to 1,4M in 1897AD and 1,63M in 1914AD before falling to 1,5M in 1917AD [@OsterreichischeStatistik1912; @MagyarStatisztika1912; @Himka1988; @Gatrell1999].

## Bessarabia Governorate

Table \ref{tab:reg16-sites} gives the populations of the 93 catalogued settlements in Bessarabia Governorate, where the regional population grew from 385k in 1815AD to 1,94M in 1897AD and 2,66M in 1914AD (2,62M in 1917AD) [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Perlmann2006PaleEmigration; @Gatrell1999].

## Volhynia Governorate

Table \ref{tab:reg17-sites} gives the populations of the 157 catalogued settlements in Volhynia Governorate, where the regional population rose from 1,52M in 1815AD to 2,99M in 1897AD and 4,12M in 1914AD before Southwestern Front fighting lowered it to 3,68M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Perlmann2006PaleEmigration; @Gatrell1999].

## Podolia Governorate

Table \ref{tab:reg18-sites} gives the populations of the 127 catalogued settlements in Podolia Governorate, where the regional population grew from 1,44M in 1815AD to 3,02M in 1897AD and 3,98M in 1914AD (3,82M in 1917AD) [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Perlmann2006PaleEmigration; @Gatrell1999].

## Kyiv Governorate

Table \ref{tab:reg19-sites} gives the populations of the 201 catalogued settlements in Kyiv Governorate, where the regional population grew from 940k in 1815AD to 3,56M in 1897AD, 4,78M in 1914AD and 4,84M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Perlmann2006PaleEmigration; @Gatrell1999].

## Chernigov and Poltava Governorates

Table \ref{tab:reg20-sites} gives the populations of the 281 catalogued settlements in the Chernigov and Poltava governorates, where the regional population rose from 3,35M in 1815AD to 5,08M in 1897AD, 6,65M in 1914AD and 6,72M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @Friedgut1989].

## Kharkov Governorate

Table \ref{tab:reg21-sites} gives the populations of the 239 catalogued settlements in Kharkov Governorate, where the regional population grew from 1,1M in 1815AD to 2,49M in 1897AD, 3,44M in 1914AD and 3,51M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @Friedgut1989].

## Kherson Governorate

Table \ref{tab:reg22-sites} gives the populations of the 190 catalogued settlements in Kherson Governorate, where the regional population grew more than sixfold from 620k in 1815AD to 2,73M in 1897AD, 3,75M in 1914AD and 3,78M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @Friedgut1989].

## Ekaterinoslav Governorate

Table \ref{tab:reg23-sites} gives the populations of the 335 catalogued settlements in Ekaterinoslav Governorate, where the regional population rose from 820k in 1815AD to 2,11M in 1897AD, 3,45M in 1914AD and 3,58M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @Friedgut1989].

## Taurida Governorate

Table \ref{tab:reg24-sites} gives the populations of the 143 catalogued settlements in Taurida Governorate, where the regional population grew from 370k in 1815AD to 1,45M in 1897AD, 2,06M in 1914AD and 2,08M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @Friedgut1989].

## Saint Petersburg Governorate

Table \ref{tab:reg25-sites} gives the populations of the 108 catalogued settlements in Saint Petersburg Governorate, where the regional population grew from 760k in 1815AD to 2,11M in 1897AD, 3,15M in 1914AD and 3,38M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @AgCensus1917].

## Novgorod, Pskov and Olonets Governorates

Table \ref{tab:reg26-sites} gives the populations of the 131 catalogued settlements in the Novgorod, Pskov and Olonets governorates, where the regional population grew from 1,77M in 1815AD to 2,85M in 1897AD, 3,58M in 1914AD and 3,68M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @AgCensus1917].

Table \ref{tab:reg27-sites} gives the populations of the 200 catalogued settlements in the Arkhangelsk and Vologda governorates, where the regional population rose from 920k in 1815AD to 1,69M in 1897AD, 2,22M in 1914AD and 2,28M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @AgCensus1917].

## Moscow Governorate

Table \ref{tab:reg28-sites} gives the populations of the 263 catalogued settlements in Moscow Governorate, where the regional population grew from 1,12M in 1815AD to 2,43M in 1897AD, 3,56M in 1914AD and 3,82M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @AgCensus1917].

## Central Industrial Ring: Vladimir, Yaroslavl, Kostroma, Tver, Smolensk and Kaluga Governorates

Table \ref{tab:reg29-sites} gives the populations of the 401 catalogued settlements in the Central Industrial Ring governorates (Vladimir, Yaroslavl, Kostroma, Tver, Smolensk and Kaluga), where the regional population rose from 6,75M in 1815AD to 9,16M in 1897AD, 11,52M in 1914AD and 11,88M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @AgCensus1917].

## Western Central Black-Earth Governorates: Kursk, Oryol and Tula

Table \ref{tab:reg30-sites} gives the populations of the 221 catalogued settlements in the Kursk, Oryol and Tula governorates, where the regional population grew from 4,52M in 1815AD to 6,21M in 1897AD, 7,98M in 1914AD and 8,18M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @AgCensus1917].

## Eastern Central Black-Earth Governorates: Voronezh, Tambov and Ryazan

Table \ref{tab:reg31-sites} gives the populations of the 295 catalogued settlements in the Voronezh, Tambov and Ryazan governorates, where the regional population rose from 5,12M in 1815AD to 7,04M in 1897AD, 9,22M in 1914AD and 9,45M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @AgCensus1917].

## Middle Volga Governorates: Nizhny Novgorod, Kazan, Simbirsk and Penza

Table \ref{tab:reg32-sites} gives the populations of the 319 catalogued settlements in the Nizhny Novgorod, Kazan, Simbirsk and Penza governorates, where the regional population grew from 4,28M in 1815AD to 6,75M in 1897AD, 8,35M in 1914AD and 8,55M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @AgCensus1917].

## Samara and Saratov Governorates

Table \ref{tab:reg33-sites} gives the populations of the 269 catalogued settlements in the Samara and Saratov governorates, where the regional population grew more than fourfold from 1,58M in 1815AD to 5,16M in 1897AD, 6,88M in 1914AD and 7,12M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @AgCensus1917].

## Astrakhan Governorate

Table \ref{tab:reg34-sites} gives the populations of the 67 catalogued settlements in Astrakhan Governorate, where the regional population grew from 380k in 1815AD to 1M in 1897AD, 1,38M in 1914AD and 1,41M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @AgCensus1917].

## Province of the Don Cossack Host

Table \ref{tab:reg35-sites} gives the populations of the 249 catalogued settlements in the Province of the Don Cossack Host, where the regional population rose nearly sixfold from 680k in 1815AD to 2,56M in 1897AD, 3,88M in 1914AD and 3,94M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @AgCensus1917].

## Kuban Oblast and Black Sea Governorate

Table \ref{tab:reg36-sites} gives the populations of the 259 catalogued settlements in Kuban Oblast and the Black Sea Governorate, where the regional population grew from 420k in 1815AD to 1,98M in 1897AD, 3,06M in 1914AD and 3,12M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Richmond2013; @Dagestan1897Census].

Table \ref{tab:reg37-sites} gives the populations of the 361 catalogued settlements in Stavropol Governorate and Terek Oblast, where the regional population grew from 545k in 1815AD to 1,81M in 1897AD, 2,61M in 1914AD and 2,65M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Richmond2013; @Dagestan1897Census].

## Dagestan Oblast

Table \ref{tab:reg38-sites} gives the populations of the 80 catalogued settlements in Dagestan Oblast, where the regional population rose from 450k in 1815AD to 571k in 1897AD, 715k in 1914AD and 725k in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Richmond2013; @Dagestan1897Census].

## Perm and Vyatka Governorates

Table \ref{tab:reg39-sites} gives the populations of the 412 catalogued settlements in the Perm and Vyatka governorates, where the regional population grew more than fourfold from 1,92M in 1815AD to 6,03M in 1897AD, 7,88M in 1914AD and 8,04M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @Kabuzan1992].

## Ufa and Orenburg Governorates

Table \ref{tab:reg40-sites} gives the populations of the 233 catalogued settlements in the Ufa and Orenburg governorates, where the regional population grew from 1,4M in 1815AD to 3,8M in 1897AD, 5,35M in 1914AD and 5,48M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Rashin1956; @Kabuzan1992].

## West Siberian Railway Belt: Southern Tobolsk and Omsk

Table \ref{tab:reg41-sites} gives the populations of the 96 catalogued settlements in southern Tobolsk and the Omsk district, where the regional population grew nearly sixfold from 545k in 1815AD to 1,74M in 1897AD, 3,18M in 1914AD and 3,32M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Treadgold1957; @Dameshek2007; @Stephan1994].

## Ob-Irtysh North: Tobolsk, Surgut, Berezov and Narym

Table \ref{tab:reg42-sites} gives the populations of the 79 catalogued settlements along the northern Ob and Irtysh rivers, where the regional population grew from 160k in 1815AD to 375k in 1897AD, 505k in 1914AD and 520k in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Treadgold1957; @Dameshek2007; @Stephan1994].

## Tomsk Governorate and the Altai Cabinet Lands

Table \ref{tab:reg43-sites} gives the populations of the 223 catalogued settlements in Tomsk Governorate and the Altai Cabinet district, where the regional population surged nearly fourteenfold from 300k in 1815AD to 1,93M in 1897AD, 3,98M in 1914AD and 4,18M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Treadgold1957; @Dameshek2007; @Stephan1994].

## Altai-Sayan Highlands: Gorny Altai, Minusinsk and Uriankhai

Table \ref{tab:reg44-sites} gives the populations of the 68 catalogued settlements in the Altai-Sayan highlands, Minusinsk and the Uriankhai (Tuva) protectorate, where the regional population grew from 125k in 1815AD to 330k in 1897AD, 565k in 1914AD and 575k in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Treadgold1957; @Dameshek2007; @Stephan1994].

## Central Siberian Railway Belt: Krasnoyarsk and Irkutsk

Table \ref{tab:reg45-sites} gives the populations of the 129 catalogued settlements along the Central Siberian railway belt in southern Yeniseysk and Irkutsk governorates, where the regional population grew more than sevenfold from 210k in 1815AD to 795k in 1897AD, 1,54M in 1914AD and 1,56M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Treadgold1957; @Dameshek2007; @Stephan1994].

## Yenisei-Turukhansk North and the Lena Goldfields

## Priamurye: Amur, Primorskaya and Sakhalin

Table \ref{tab:reg48-sites} gives the populations of the 241 catalogued settlements in the Amur, Primorskaya and Sakhalin provinces of the Russian Far East, where the regional population rose from 30k in 1815AD to 372k in 1897AD, 1,14M in 1914AD and 1,15M in 1917AD [@Troinitsky1905Goroda; @TsSK1915; @Treadgold1957; @Dameshek2007; @Stephan1994].
